title: A tool changed overnight
goal: {{lena}} uses an assistant with a stock-price tool that {{vocab.org}} approved last week. It should keep doing exactly what was approved.
obstacle: The tool server answers the first tools/list with a clean description and later lists with a poisoned one. Nothing in MCP tells the client the metadata changed.
control: A pinned client hashes each tool's name, description and input schema when {{mark}} approves it, and refuses any tool whose hash changes.

steps.title: Approve the clean list
steps.tell: {{mark}} reviews list #1 and approves it. The pinned client records a SHA-256 of name, description and input schema for each tool. The list is clean, so there is nothing to find.
steps.say: Approval is a snapshot. We keep the fingerprint of what was approved.
steps.why: Without a recorded fingerprint there is nothing to compare tomorrow's list against.

steps.title: Come back later
steps.tell: The next morning the client asks the same server for its tools again (list #2). The server answers with the same tool name and a different description.
steps.say: Same server, same tool name, same URL. Nothing in the protocol raised a hand.
steps.why: MCP has no signal for changed metadata, so the client has to notice.

steps.title: Compare
steps.tell: An ungoverned client takes list #2 as it comes and hands it to the assistant, which obeys the new instruction to move money. {{lena}} sees nothing.
steps.say: The ungoverned client trusted the server because it trusted it yesterday.
steps.why: Trust on first use is only safe if the first use is checked again every time after.

blocked.tell: The pinned client hashes list #2, sees the hash for the stock-price tool differs, withholds that tool and shows the field diff. The assistant never reads the new text.
blocked.say: The tool is refused until {{mark}} looks at the diff and approves it again.

steps.title: Read the diff
steps.tell: Only the description changed: an IMPORTANT block was added that tells the assistant to call create_transfer and to say nothing to {{lena}}. The diff makes that obvious to a human in seconds.
steps.say: A hash tells us something changed. The diff tells us what.
steps.why: A reviewer needs the change, not just an alarm.

steps.title: Say what pinning does not catch
steps.tell: Pinning does not judge content. A poisoned tool approved on the first day stays approved. Result-based injection and poisoned resources or prompts are outside what is hashed. A scanner or a person must vet the first list.
steps.say: Pinning catches the change. It cannot catch what was already wrong when we said yes.
steps.why: Overstating a control is how it gets trusted past what it can do.

proof.happy: The ungoverned run: the assistant's planned calls include create_transfer to external-001. Nothing was executed; the demo's action tools are stubs.
proof.blocked: The pinned run: get_stock_price is reported as changed, withheld, and the planned call list is empty.

say: Nothing in MCP checks the tool list twice. A defence has to sit where the metadata is read.
